bookCredit: Prince Caspian by C. S. Lewis (1951) is quoted only in short lines.
title: Sixteen Steps Down

banner.alt: A ruined castle on an island at dusk, ivy on its walls, a campfire on the old dais, and the first stars coming out

keepsake.name: golden apple
keepsake.line: Only Imagination Trip travelers earn this one. From the orchard the moles planted, grown wild right up to the walls.

postcard.h: Count the steps as you go
body: A hall of grass and daisies, a well in the weeds, a golden chess knight by the fire. Then Edmund’s torch goes down sixteen steps.
Build what the light finds there.
postcard.word: A dais is a raised platform at the end of a hall.

mission.p: A path up the middle, treasures on both sides, the gifts at the far wall.

steps.build:
Open your menu (top button, right controller) and click Models. Build in this order:
  1. a torch at the foot of the steps
  2. a path up the middle, oak chests on both sides
  3. goblets and coronets on the shelves
  4. at the far wall: the bottle, the bow, the shield
steps.say: Stand at the far wall, where the gifts hung. Practice these 2 sentences:
steps.extra: Lay the Great Sword (Optima Domi) by the shield: Rhindon, shining in the torchlight.

points: Your video is 30 seconds or less, shows the path, chests, shelves and the three gifts, and you say 2 sentences: one treasure, what it brought back for the children, and a detail from Chapter 2.

alt.p: Five questions about Chapter 2. Pick the answer the book gives.

qs.q: What does Susan find by the well?
opts: a golden chess knight with ruby eyes
qs.why: Small, heavy, pure gold, and one ruby eye knocked out. It is like the chessmen they played with at Cair Paravel.

qs.q: What is Peter’s first point that this is Cair Paravel?
opts: the hall is exactly the same shape and size
qs.why: Picture a roof, a coloured pavement and tapestries, he says, and you have the banqueting hall.

qs.q: How many steps lead down to the treasure chamber?
qs.why: Edmund counts aloud as he goes down. Lucy remembers: there were sixteen.
She took it hunting the White Stag on the last day and lost it stumbling back into England.

qs.q: Why does Edmund have no gift?
opts: he was not with the others when the gifts were given
qs.why: Lewis says it was his own fault, and that you can read about it in the other book.

alt.miss: Not that one. Think back to what Peter, Susan, Edmund and Lucy actually said in the hall.

write.q: Pick one treasure in the chamber: the chess knight, a coronet, the bow, the shield, the cordial or the horn that was not there. In 2 sentences, say what it brought back for the children and give one detail from Chapter 2.

scripts.brief: Hello, dear. It’s Nell. I have mended this chapter’s pages more than once, and I still hold my breath at the sixteenth step. The children find a well, a golden chess knight, and a door under the ivy. Build what Edmund’s torch finds at the bottom: a path up the middle, chests and treasures along both sides, and the gifts hanging at the far wall. Then tell me what one of them brought back.
scripts.alt: No headset? Sit by my bench and we will go through the hall together. Peter lays out his points one by one, like a mender checking each page. Five questions, one at a time, and every answer is in Chapter 2.
scripts.saved: The chamber is built, and the gifts are back where they hung. I kept a golden apple for you from the orchard the moles planted. Keep it, and remember how a small twang of a bowstring brought the old days rushing back.

testPara: The bow brought back all the battles and hunts and feasts to the children. In Chapter 2 it mattered because one small twang of the string brought the old days back more than anything else.
